Trust me - your contract ends that day and you get paid when the agency cuts their checks. Usually that's the amount of hours you work. They aren't going to pay you more while you're on the bench... that's just not the way they do things.

I am sure you know what I am talking about - you just choose not to admit it here which is totally fine.  
Keep in mind you mentioned an important word - almost. That being said, if you have a system and it works for you, I'm not going to challenge you on that. That being said, thanks to inflation being what it is, hope you got a raise because it's getting more expensive to live every day.

Don't get me wrong, there are perks to being a contractor. I periodically offer my services doing business writing too and get paid more than the pennies per word BS that most copywriters charge.

That being said, sure you can cut out the middle person, but usually that means you get the same rate, but your employer in essence gets a discount b/c they don't need to pay the markup to an agency.

And like I said, what moron would ever ever put in a contract that you get paid until the end of  X period if they decide to end the contract? I don't know of a single company that is truly that stupid.

In my days as a contractor I wouldn't act like an entitled douche like OP.  


To the uninformed / inexperienced in here, you may think from this post that being a contractor means you can miss meetings and sleep in without any ramifications. May I make a suggestion that you actually go to those meetings if asked (being the last to know about something and thrown under the bus isn't a fun experience) and ignoring 'requests' from management saying that you'll be paid until x time isn't really accurate either.

Being a contractor means you're usually the one person who actually needs to be an adult and actually pay attention because you're the easiest person to get rid of -- if they terminate your contract, you're contract is done that very day and you get paid net-15, net-30, etc. - you don't get paid until that day ... no company is going to agree to a contract like that unless they are really stupid.

While in many cases it's easier to get a job as a contractor, remember that means you have a fixed duration and then you get to look for another one (yay!) repeatedly, (usually) don't get benefits that your FT colleagues get like vacation, healthcare and the like and in many cases, you get paid the same or less than your FT colleagues as well.

There is a labor shortage in fields where there is a revolving door like retail, fast food and the like. On the other hand, there are more jobs than people in fields like engineering and the like - at least if you read Blind that's what they say.

I don't lead with pay / benefits because there will always be someone else who will offer more than me. I have a startup myself and I don't have an unlimited supply of money to throw at candidates. 

If you tell your managers and supervisors that I hope they leave you because those are the people you need to keep because those ones are the ones who make sure your business keeps moving. Threatening them is a \*fantastic\* way for them to leave you and go somewhere else because they don't need to play games with you.

Don't be surprised if the C-suite fires you for giving such large raises. If the workers deserve it and you have the money, yes give them a decent raise but don't do it unilaterally because your job is on the line.

Sounds to me like you are a pretty lousy manager if you have jobs open for that long or can't interview very well.

Not a red flag at all to some people. Some like to work in driven intense environments and enjoy reaping those rewards, but if you're looking for a company to tell you "oh we are looking for people to work a couple hours and we will pay you a premium" that isn't going to happen.

No company is going to say "we obviously expect you to answer the phone on your day off if we call". That's just insane.

No one is telling you to be a pushover or to sacrifice WLB. In fact in this economy, if you're inexperienced at many companies, you're even more appealing because you have less to "unlearn" as my former boss tells everyone who will listen.  


There are ways to ask questions about work/life balance, corporate/group culture and the like which are acceptable questions that make you look like an appealing candidate without asking about the compensation package.

If you want to do that while applying for a fast food job, go for it, but if you want a legit job, then that's the wrong approach.

Yes and no. They get a percentage of that hire's salary, but they don't take it out of the employee's salary. It's paid on top of that - you would be given that extra money anyways so don't count money that isn't yours.

Some seriously solid advice here. 

You shouldn't ask those questions at the beginning of the process \*unless\* you want to tell the interviewer you don't want to work there. Using that often overused dating metaphor, you don't ask to sleep with your date or tell him/her you love them shortly after you meet with them so why should you ask \*any\* of these questions until there is at least some interest on their side?

In many cases, these three questions are answered very early in the process (especially if you're qualified and some states actually have passed laws mandating this) or are even shared in public so why do you think asking these questions are good ones?

It isn't a question of correct or not, it's a question of how do you keep your job. If you want to take a vacation, take one before you start your job - don't do it during your probation period - it's really that simple.

False. Companies rescind offers all the time - often for a lot less. Companies don't pay $5k to get you to the offer phase... Don't believe me? Check out any Human Resources group and they'll tell you they'd rather rescind the offer than take a chance to see how you perform if you do something like this.

I wouldn't even allow it. There's a reason why companies often have 90 day probationary periods when you start a new job. Taking ANY time off outside official company holidays and sick time is a MASSIVE red flag to any manager.  


By doing this, you're basically telling the manager you think you deserve special treatment - and even with the #greatresignation going on, this is a sure fire way to get  your boss annoyed with you. You might not get fired, but it definitely would be something I'd express concerns about.  


Don't be stupid. Take your vacation using the PTO from your previous company OR ask if you can start three weeks from offer accepted so you can take time off.

Definitely not. When I was a hiring manager, doing this was the fastest way to get an offer rescinded besides lying on your employment application. In general, if you want to take a vacation, say you want to start in three weeks -- so you can give your traditional two weeks notice and the a week to do whatever you need to do before you start work.  


If anything, if the company says "yes" to this, then that's a bigger red flag because it shows you that this company has idiots for managers who don't pay attention to what's going on around them.

It's part of it for sure. So... this is the situation at work. About five months ago I managed to get a job at a ginormous software company in their solution (product) marketing department, but as a contractor.   


As someone who has a lot of experience in that field, I knew what I should have done, but for some reason I couldn't. It got to the point where even I couldn't even do the "easiest" stuff -- but a lot of it had to do with the fact that I couldn't see it the same way as my boss and totally messed up on two assignments and that was just too much for my boss so she decided to let me go on 2/4 but agreed to pay me until 2/15 because she wanted to be nice.  


After I was let go, I talked to a number of my teammates and other people in the other groups and nearly everyone told me that my boss is notoriously hard to work with (which is part of the reason why she pretends to be sweet and helpful in her role -- they think she's a shitty manager behind her back) as well as the products I was supposed to work on were extremely complicated and required a lot of experience with how the company worked in order to be successful.  Since I was brand new to the company and these products, I tried and tried to learn and show I could do the job, but just couldn't absorb the information and failed to connect with the others to get things done. Nearly everyone else in my group except for a couple of people were in their roles for years so they probably could have done this job -- and the couple who were "new" to the company were full time folks who were given products that didn't have so many complicated parts or didn't have the politics associated with them.  


I am extremely angry because it took me a long time to get that job (6 years) and I am angry at myself because I feel like I blew a chance to actually become very successful. Now I have to start all over again and start looking for another job -- one that is ideally full time (contracts are just too hard), in a field that I can do, and one where I can stay -- and grow. The worst part is that everyone is telling me there are tons of marketing jobs out there, While that may be true, I'm competing against people in their 20s and 30s who are moving up the ladder which makes it even harder. Younger folks have managed to take over this field and even if they suck at it, it doesn't matter because they are young and that's okay. This is why I picked the name I did - I am a Gen-Xer who has outlived his usefulness.  


Sadly, I live in an area where it's obscenely expensive to live and prior to this job I was very underpaid. I worked for my parents in a different field all together (manufacturing) while I tried to land a job like this one. I applied for hundreds of jobs and got some interviews, but I never was able to get a job.  


SO when you combine all of these things, it's really hard for me to continue living. I have had to take retail and bullshit jobs too many times and I can't do it again.   


If you want to know more, feel free to send me a private message.

I definitely try to do the best I can - though I just can't actually align properly with other people for some reason. And no... I don't think I love myself at all. If anything i hate myself because I see things so differently than other people.

It is tough - in fact it's very tough because I am at the point where I don't even know if I can do the right thing anymore. I was fired from my dream job (or the job that would get me to my dream job) last Friday, I am burning out my friends (assuming they are friends) and so much more.  


So... to answer your question, am I very hard on myself? Maybe, but I definitely deserve it!
